items.title: The allegations against the Greens’ Jordon Steele-John – podcast
items.standfirst: Greens senator for Western Australia, Jordon Steele-John, has blamed ‘nasty political games’ for the timing of allegations of misconduct towards women spanning nearly a decade. items.content: Greens leader David Shoebridge has insisted that Senator Jordon Steele-John should take personal leave, after the WA senator denied he had offered or agreed to step back while allegations against him were investigated.

items.title: David Shoebridge responds to Jordon Steele-John’s explosive statement as Greens hold emergency meeting
items.standfirst: The new Greens leader says it is his understanding the Western Australian senator ‘agreed’ to take leave from the party roomGet our new political email, free app or daily news podcastThe Greens leader, David Shoebridge, has said it was his understanding Jordon Steele-John agreed to take leave from parliament while misconduct allegations against him are investigated, and that it is “appropriate” that he does so, despite the Western Australian senator saying overnight that he was not on leave and had never agreed to stay away from parliament.Steele-John released a lengthy, explosive statement on Sunday night claiming Shoebridge pressured him to take leave after complaints about his conduct were made public last week, and accused an internal faction within the Greens of playing “nasty political games”. He has denied any allegations of misconduct. Continue reading...
